title: runtime-benchmarking-harness-and-regression-notes
body:
Purpose:
This doc is a working draft for the runtime benchmarking harness and a running log of recent perf regressions (microbenchmarks + traces). Audience: serving-runtime engineers, QE, and applied-ML infra. Goal: capture the harness design, test matrix, observed regressions, root-cause hypotheses, and short-term mitigation steps so we can iterate quickly and keep regressions actionable.

High-level requirements for the harness:
- Reproducible microbench suites that run deterministically on the same AMI/container image
- Token-level tracing to measure: enqueue->dispatch latency, kernel queue wait, kernel execution, memcpy, kv-cache lookup/update, post-processing
- Configurable test matrix: model family (llama2/opt/gpt), seq length, batch size, temperature, decoding mode (greedy/beam/streaming), quantization (fp16, int8, nf4)
body_continued:
- Kernel variant toggles: fused_attention, flash_attn2, triton-custom, cutlass-cu -- ability to pin kernel per op for A/B tests
- Scheduler scenarios: single-request latency, steady-state throughput, bursty arrivals (Poisson+bursts), backpressure handling, resource contention with mixed-model workloads
- KV cache focused tests: cold-start vs warm-cache, cache-hit ratio sweeps, concurrent KV writes and reads, cache-eviction scenarios
- Lightweight alerting: regression thresholds, automatic git-bisect candidate collection, and links to perf traces when thresholds are tripped

Harness architecture (draft):
- runner/bench-runner (python/Go): orchestrates runs, mounts metrics collectors, uploads artifacts to GCS
- microbench suites (pytest-style): micro_attention.py, kv_cache_ops.py, matmul_kernels.py, dispatch_scheduler.py
- trace collectors: CUPTI probe wrapper for CUDA kernels, eBPF for kernel queue events, token-level instrumentation in the serving runtime (span ids forwarded to tracing backend)
- results storage: JSON artifacts + compressed pprof/nvprof traces stored per-run with run metadata (git SHA, docker image, instance type, exact kernel flags)

Test matrix (example canonical runs):
- Model: llama-2-13b, batch sizes: [1,4,8], seq lengths: [16,128,512], quant: [fp16, nf4], kernel variants: [flash_attn, triton_opt]
- Hardware: A100-40GB (p4d), A10G (g4dn-like), H100 (where available)
- SLO/thresholds (initial): 95th latency for single token decode < 20ms on A100-batch1-seq16; throughput target >= 200 tokens/s for llama-2-13b batch8-seq128 under steady-state

Recent microbench results (selected runs):
- 2024-10-12 / run-id: run-20241012-17:30 / image: bench:v2024-10-09 / HW: A100-40GB
  - flash_attn: batch1-seq16: median=7.2ms, p95=12.9ms, throughput=420 tok/s
  - triton_opt: batch1-seq16: median=9.6ms, p95=18.4ms, throughput=320 tok/s
  - kv-cache cold-start write latency: median=0.9ms, kv-hit ratio artificially 0.0
  Notes: flash_attn wins on small seq lengths as expected.

- 2024-10-19 / run-id: run-20241019-09:04 / image: bench:v2024-10-17 / HW: A100-40GB
  - flash_attn: batch8-seq128: median=35ms, p95=72ms, throughput=230 tok/s
  - regression observed vs baseline (2024-09-21): p95 increased from 60ms -> 72ms (~20% regression)
body_continued_2:
Trace analysis (2024-10-19):
- Token-level trace shows increased kernel queue wait time (median queue wait jumped from 6ms -> 14ms). Kernel execution time stable.
- nvprof/CUPTI reveals sporadic memcpy stalls on device-to-device transfers around KV cache serializing: writes batched differently when concurrent requests increased.
- Hypothesis: Scheduler packing policy change (PR #812) introduced different batch composition for concurrent sequences resulting in more fragmented kernel invocations and extra memcpy syncs.

Action items from regression:
- Reproduce on smaller controlled harness with synthetic workload hitting the packing policy path (assigned: Riley). Target date: 2024-10-24.
- Add a microbench that isolates D2D memcpy patterns during KV writes and measures tls/stream synchronization points (assigned: Miguel).
- Revert the packing policy in a canary build for a small customer (if reproduces locally) and run bench suite (assigned: Priya + EngOps).
- Add automatic detection: when p95 latency increases >10% vs baseline for same run-config, collect full CUPTI trace and link to Jira.

KV-cache specific notes:
- Observed behavior: warm hits are fast (~0.3ms lookup). Mixed reads/writes under concurrent requests create short-lived stream syncs adding ~1-8ms per token in certain runs.
- Implementation detail suspected: current KV writer uses a mutex across shards during compaction which can hold a host-to-device memcpy in-flight. We should:
  1) audit the writer lock scope and avoid holding it across the memcpy
  2) switch to per-shard write buffers and async submits tied to CUDA streams
  3) expose a runtime flag to disable compaction during high-concurrency workloads

Kernel selection & scheduling observations:
- Kernel bench harness must support per-op kernel pinning so we can compare fused vs unfused variants on identical scheduling decisions.
- We currently observe that the kernel chooser heuristic prefers lower-launch-overhead kernels for seq<32. This interacts badly with new packer because it mixes seq16 and seq64 requests.
- Proposed short-term mitigation: update packer to group by preferred kernel type (heuristic: kernel_preference_key = model_variant + seq_bucket + quant_profile) so kernels launched are more homogeneous.

Trace handling and storage:
- Keep 1-week hot trace retention, 3-month cold artifacts (compressed). Attach run metadata: git_sha, docker_tag, instance_type, random-seed, bench-config yml.
- Traces must include mapping: request-id -> token-level spans -> kernel-span (with kernel-name, stream-id) -> memcpy spans.

Regression runbook (sketch):
1) Triage: collect bench run JSON, pprof, CUPTI trace, scheduler dump.
2) Quick checks: did kernel execution time change? (if yes, inspect kernel code changes)
3) If kernel exec stable but queue wait increased: check packing/scheduler PRs between baseline and current SHA.
4) If memcpy stalls: focus on KV cache writer/reader commits or tensor re-sharding changes.
5) Run targeted microbench (kv-memcpy-iso) to confirm.
6) If reproduced: bisect commits on the serving-runtime tree and open JIRA with everything attached.

Open questions / TODOs:
- What thresholding is reasonable to auto-trigger a bisect job? p95 > 10% across 3 consecutive runs? or absolute delta e.g., >5ms? Need product input on acceptable risk windows.
- Expand microbench coverage to include batch preemption cases and prefetch interleaving.
- Add synthetic multi-model mixed workloads to simulate platform customers running many model flavors concurrently.
- Work with SRE to run benchmark suite in CI on a quarterly cadence with strict artifact collection.

Notes to self / engineering shorthand (informal):
- bench scripts under tools/perf/bench_runner.py – wrapper accepts --pin-kernel, --seq-buckets, --kv-async=true/false
- use bench-image: registry.redwood/bench:20241009 for reproductions
- Handy grep: grep -R "pack.*policy" serving-runtime/packers/ – quick pointer to the packing PR that likely started this regression (PR#812).

Appendix: relevant links and raw snippets
- perf PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/812
- bisect candidate starter command: tools/perf/bisect_helper.sh --metric p95 --baseline sha=abc123 --target sha=def456 --run-config configs/llama13b-basic.yml
- Example run JSON keys we collect: run_id, git_sha, docker_tag, hw_type, metrics:{median,p95,p99,throughput}, trace_paths:[...], bench_notes

End of draft.

Revision history:
- 2024-09-18 initial sketch (Asha)
